text: You could add 40, ten times.
That works. But it takes a while, and it's easy to lose count.
Is there a faster way? Yes. It's in this chart of places.
Slide a digit left and it's worth 10 times as much, slide it right and it's worth one tenth as much.
Look at the places, from the right.
10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. 10 hundreds make 1 thousand.
See the pattern? Each step to the left is 10 times as much.
Look at 40. The 4 is in the tens place.
Slide it one place to the left, into the hundreds. That's 400.
That's 10 times as much. So a carton holds 400 pencils.
Now go back the other way. One box is one tenth of a carton.
Slide the 4 in 400 one place to the right, back to the tens. That's 40.
So one tenth of 400 is 40 pencils.
Here's the part people mix up.

text: Add 37 one thousand times? That would take all day.
There's a faster way. And it works for dividing too.
Each zero in 10, 100 or 1,000 slides every digit one place, left to multiply and right to divide.
Start with 10. It has one zero.
So 37 times 10 slides the 3 and the 7 one place to the left.
The ones place is empty now, so a zero fills it. That's 370.
Now 100. It has two zeros, so the digits slide two places. That's 3,700.
1,000 has three zeros, so they slide three places. That's 37,000.
So the shop has 37,000 beads.
Now go backwards. The shop shares 37,000 beads into 1,000 bags.
1,000 still has three zeros. So every digit slides three places — this time to the right.
The zeros slide off the end. That's 37 beads in each bag.
When you divide, don't slide LEFT.
Dividing makes the number smaller, so every digit slides right.
A carton of pencils. A box holds 40 pencils. A carton holds 10 boxes. How many pencils are in a carton?
Boxes of beads. Every box on the shelf holds 37 beads. The craft shop has 1,000 boxes. How many beads is that?
Now you try. In 70, the 7 is in the tens place. What is the 7 worth if it slides one place to the left? Find the place one step to the left. It's worth 10 times as much.
Now you try. Multiply. 45 times 1,000 equals what? Count the zeros. Slide every digit that many places.
Which place is one step to the left of the tens?
One place to the left is worth 10 times as much. So what is 10 times 7 tens?
Which place is one step to the left of the hundreds?
One place to the left is worth 10 times as much. So what is 10 times 3 hundreds?
How many zeros does 1,000 have? That is how many places to slide.
Multiplying slides the digits to the left. Slide the 4 and the 5 three places, then fill the empty places with zeros.
How many zeros does 100 have? That is how many places to slide.
Multiplying slides the digits to the left. Slide the 2 and the 9 two places, then fill the empty places with zeros.
Try a new one. In 300, the 3 is in the hundreds place. What is the 3 worth if it slides one place to the left?
Try a new one. Multiply. 29 times 100 equals what?
You did it! You slid the 7 one place to the left, and now it's worth 10 times as much.
Yes! You slid the 3 one place to the left, from 300 all the way to 3,000.
You watched how it works, step by step. The practice problems will help it stick.
